items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I mean Coltrane. Because the energy and the feeling you get from the recorded medium is phenomenal but that never approaches what it’s like to be in the room. ... And to get to play with them would have been an astounding treat.

ctx.x: I mean it’s something else, right? It’s making connections between players, and I mean I don’t know what. But maybe we can’t describe it but you’re feeling it in the last year or so you said.

I just feel like I’m getting a better idea about music and projecting that other thing which can’t really be described or explained. You know it’s not a technical thing. It’s not necessarily an intellectual thing. It’s more a vibe that’s being created and maybe you want to call it a spiritual kind of feeling. But projecting a feeling and having people being able to feel something through the music. I mean I realize that recently this is a gift if you can play music and get out there and play for people.
